securityClaim: No system is 100% secure. This policy targets standards-aligned quantum readiness using free/open-source tooling.
minimumTlsVersionComment: TLSv1.3 is a required hardening target, not evidence of deployed enforcement. On 2026-10-16, certificate-verified legacy-capable probes negotiated TLS 1.0/1.1 and received HTTP 200 from dip82eloip5zb.cloudfront.net, correcting the prior false-negative measurement. OpenSSL client-side ERR_SSL_NO_PROTOCOLS_AVAILABLE must not count as server rejection. The backend origin rejected both legacy versions; CloudFront and the origin each accepted TLS 1.3 with only X25519MLKEM768 offered. This proves optional hybrid handshake capability, not full-path PQC. CloudFront's default certificate forces the TLSv1 viewer policy; no owned domain or us-east-1 ACM certificate was found in this AWS account. CloudFront origin API values currently stop at TLSv1.2; that configured minimum alone does not establish the negotiated origin protocol. Keep the legacy-rejection and TLS 1.3-only gates strict while these deployment limits remain unresolved.
forbiddenNewCrypto: RSA publicEncrypt/privateDecrypt for application payload encryption
warningCrypto: third-party SDK crypto outside direct app control
productionRules: Do not deploy experimental OQS/liboqs TLS directly to production without staging evidence.
Keep rollback to classical TLS 1.3 possible.
Never invent a cryptographic primitive; application-layer composition must use standardized primitives with documented domain separation.

runtimePqc.notes: Application-layer hybrid PQC is implemented with native Node 24.7+/OpenSSL 3.5+ primitives and is opt-in. Field encryption and the security event ledger default to their classical modes so an unconfigured deployment cannot fail closed on a runtime that lacks FIPS 203/204 support. Production rollout requires explicit key references and the require mode.
